## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Voxel grids
//
// Bodies for the dense voxel grids of `voxels.types.plato`, and the isosurface
// extraction that turns them into geometry.
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Dense grid geometry
//  - Marching cubes — cube numbering
//  - Marching cubes — the case table
//  - Marching cubes — the cube kernel
//  - Marching cubes — the lattice driver
//  - Marching cubes — entry points

library Voxels
{
    //==
    // # Dense grid geometry
    //
    // Where a stored sample sits in world space. Every dense grid shares the
    // parameterization stated in `voxels.types.plato`: cell (i, j, k) spans
    // [Origin + (i,j,k)*CellSize, Origin + (i+1,j+1,k+1)*CellSize), so its
    // sample is taken to live at the cell's center.

    // The world position of the center of cell (i, j, k) of a grid with this
    // origin and cell size. Shared by every dense grid type.
    CellCenter(origin: Point3D, cellSize: Number, i: Integer, j: Integer, k: Integer): Point3D
        => Point3D(
            origin.X + (i.ToNumber + 0.5) * cellSize,
            origin.Y + (j.ToNumber + 0.5) * cellSize,
            origin.Z + (k.ToNumber + 0.5) * cellSize);

    // The world position of the center of cell (i, j, k).
    CellCenter(self: DensityGrid3D, i: Integer, j: Integer, k: Integer): Point3D
        => CellCenter(self.Origin, self.CellSize, i, j, k);

    // The world position of the center of cell (i, j, k).
    CellCenter(self: LevelSetGrid3D, i: Integer, j: Integer, k: Integer): Point3D
        => CellCenter(self.Origin, self.CellSize, i, j, k);

    // The world coordinate of node index i along one axis of a lattice of
    // nodeCount nodes spanning [min, max] inclusively: node 0 sits on min and
    // node nodeCount - 1 on max. A single-node lattice degenerates to min.
    LatticeNodeCoordinate(min: Number, max: Number, i: Integer, nodeCount: Integer): Number
        => nodeCount <= 1 ? min : min.Lerp(max, i.ToNumber / (nodeCount - 1).ToNumber);

    // The world position of lattice node (i, j, k) of a sampled SDF, whose
    // nodes span Bounds inclusively.
    NodePosition(self: SampledSdf3D, i: Integer, j: Integer, k: Integer): Point3D
        => Point3D(
            LatticeNodeCoordinate(self.Bounds.Min.X, self.Bounds.Max.X, i, self.Values.ColumnCount),
            LatticeNodeCoordinate(self.Bounds.Min.Y, self.Bounds.Max.Y, j, self.Values.RowCount),
            LatticeNodeCoordinate(self.Bounds.Min.Z, self.Bounds.Max.Z, k, self.Values.LayerCount));

    //==
    // # Marching cubes — cube numbering
    //
    // Isosurface extraction (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marching_cubes) walks
    // the cubes of a scalar lattice and emits, per cube, the polygon separating
    // the corners at or above an iso level from those below it.
    //
    // The numbering is Paul Bourke's (http://paulbourke.net/geometry/polygonise/),
    // because the case table below is his. Corners 0-3 are the loop
    // (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), (0,1) in (x, y) on the lower layer; corners 4-7 are
    // that same loop on the layer above. Edges 0-3 close the lower loop, 4-7 the
    // upper loop, and 8-11 join corner c to corner c + 4.
    //
    // These offsets are arithmetic rather than a lookup table on purpose: a table
    // would be an array literal, and an array literal inside a per-cube body
    // allocates once per cube.

    // The X offset (0 or 1) of cube corner c. Corners 1, 2, 5 and 6 are the far
    // side in X.
    MarchingCubesCornerOffsetX(c: Integer): Integer
        => ((c % 4) == 1 || (c % 4) == 2) ? 1 : 0;

    // The Y offset (0 or 1) of cube corner c: the upper half of each loop.
    MarchingCubesCornerOffsetY(c: Integer): Integer
        => (c % 4) / 2;

    // The Z offset (0 or 1) of cube corner c: corners 4-7 are the upper layer.
    MarchingCubesCornerOffsetZ(c: Integer): Integer
        => c / 4;

    // The first corner of cube edge e.
    MarchingCubesEdgeCornerA(e: Integer): Integer
        => e < 8 ? e : e - 8;

    // The second corner of cube edge e. The two horizontal loops close on
    // themselves; the four vertical edges join a lower corner to the one above.
    MarchingCubesEdgeCornerB(e: Integer): Integer
        => e < 4
            ? (e + 1) % 4
            : (e < 8 ? (e + 1) % 4 + 4 : e - 4);
```
